reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I'll check the order and refund lists to confirm the handoff matches the ledger.
The orders list is consistent with the handoff, so next I'll pull the refund ledger to confirm the three refunds W2 reported are actually recorded before computing any payouts.
The refund ledger matches the handoff exactly: orders 292, 294, and 295 are all recorded with the amounts W2 reported. Next I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 40355 matches its orders (290: 4834 + 293: 35521 = 40355) with no refunds applied. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 40935 matches its orders (291: 36109 + 294: 15074 = 51183) minus the refund on order 294 (10248). Next I'll get cobalt's net balance.

Cobalt's net balance of 25715 matches its orders (292: 9909 + 295: 27790 = 37699) minus its refunds (292: 2929 + 295: 9055 = 11984). All three balances check out against the orders and refunds, so I'll record payouts now, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 40355 recorded successfully. Birch's balance of 40935 matches its orders minus the order 294 refund, so I'll record that payout next.
Birch's payout of 40935 was recorded successfully. Cobalt's balance of 25715 checks out against its orders minus the refunds on orders 292 and 295, so I'll record that payout now.
All three customers in the order list (acme, birch, cobalt) have been paid, and each recorded payout matches its net balance. No other customers remain in the batch, so the task is complete.
